findings.title: AblationStudies.py (Appendix D.3 ablation figures) is referenced but absent from the repo
findings.claim: The README lists AblationStudies.py in the repo structure (line 80), in the Reproduction Roadmap (line 99: `python AblationStudies.py` -> ./results_ablation), and in the 'Ablation Studies' section (line 230), stating it reproduces the Appendix D.3 ablations and outputs Time_Embedding_Figure_12.pdf, Sensitivity_t_Figure_13.pdf and Noise_Injection_Figure_14.pdf; the file does not exist in the repository (`ls *.py` returns only AggregateResults.py, ContaminationStudies.py, FullExperiments.py, ProcessContamination.py, RobustnessStudy.py, utils.py).
findings.concern: The ablation/sensitivity results the paper uses to justify its design choices (Figures 12, 13, 14 and, with no other generating script, Figures 16/17/18 and the epoch-sensitivity Figure 5) have no code in the repo, so they cannot be reproduced.
findings.resolution: Authors: please add AblationStudies.py (and any script generating Figures 16–18 / Figure 5), or point to where these figures are produced.

findings.title: Unsupervised (CSM) epoch-selection procedure is not in the repo; epochs are hardcoded per dataset
findings.quote:
elif "skin" in dataset_name:
    epoch_size = 110  # Chosen first from "100 or 1"
    batch_size = 1024
    learning_rate = 0.005
elif "celeba" in dataset_name:
    epoch_size = 2  # Chosen first from "100 or 1"
    batch_size = 1024
    learning_rate = 0.005
findings.claim: TCCM's number of training epochs — described by the paper as 'the only data-dependent hyperparameter' and selected by an unsupervised, label-free Improved-Contrast-Score-Margin (CSM) procedure (Appendix B.6) — is instead provided as a hardcoded per-dataset if/else in determine_FMAD_hyperparameters, with comments such as `# Chosen first from "100 or 1"`; a repo-wide grep for the selection procedure (CSM / candidate / inlier / epoch-selection) finds no implementation.
findings.concern: The paper states the epochs are 'not arbitrarily hardcoded' and chosen without anomaly labels, but the repo contains only the final numbers and no selection code, so the fairness/reproducibility of TCCM's sole tuned hyperparameter (range 1–5000 epochs across datasets) cannot be verified, and the manual-looking comments suggest hand-selection rather than the described automated procedure.
findings.resolution: Authors: please release the CSM-based epoch-selection script (or the code from Li et al. 2025b as invoked here) and confirm the epochs were chosen using only training/model outputs, never test AUROC.
findings.paper_ref: Appendix B.6 'Unsupervised Epoch Selection Strategy'; Sec. B.3 ('not arbitrarily hardcoded')

findings.title: bash_files/run_knn.sh calls non-existent Full_experiments.py (actual file: FullExperiments.py)
findings.claim: run_knn.sh invokes `python Full_experiments.py` on lines 28, 63, 101 and 141, but the repository file is named FullExperiments.py (no underscore, capital E); every invocation would fail with 'can't open file Full_experiments.py'.
findings.concern: The auxiliary KNN reproduction script cannot run as written; a reviewer following it verbatim gets a file-not-found error.
findings.resolution: Rename the invocation to FullExperiments.py (the main run_main.sh already uses the correct name).

findings.title: Main benchmark has no held-out normal test set: the entire normal training set is reused as test normals
findings.quote:
X_train = X_normal.copy()
y_train = y_normal.copy()
X_test_normal = X_normal.copy()
y_test_normal = y_normal.copy()

# Test set contains both normal and abnormal data
X_test = np.vstack((X_test_normal, X_anomalous))
y_test = np.concatenate((y_test_normal, y_anomalous))
findings.claim: load_adbench_npz (used by FullExperiments.py:221 for every main-benchmark run) sets both X_train and X_test_normal to X_normal.copy(), so the normal half of X_test is byte-identical to X_train; the test set is a superset of the training set on the normal class. The `test_size=0.5`/`random_state` arguments and the imported `train_test_split` are never used. My check (_audit_code/out/split_overlap.csv) confirms 100% of training rows recur in the test set for every dataset examined (e.g. 42_WBC: 213 train normals, all 213 in a 223-row test set; 32_shuttle: 45586/45586).
findings.concern: The paper states the main protocol is 'a stratified split to the normal data, using 50% for training and holding out the rest for testing' and frames TCCM as inductive scoring 'unseen test data', but the reported AUROC/AUPRC (Figure 2) are computed with all normals seen during training, so a high-capacity model that memorises training normals (TCCM trains up to 5000 epochs on some datasets) is scored partly in-sample, inflating separation from anomalies and making the numbers non-reproducible under the described held-out protocol.
findings.resolution: Authors: re-run the main benchmark with the 50% held-out normal split that ContaminationStudies.py:168 already implements, and report whether the Figure-2 rankings and absolute AUROC/AUPRC hold; confirm which loader produced the paper's numbers.
findings.paper_ref: Sec. 4 'Experimental Setup, (2) Data Processing' (50% train / hold out rest); Sec. 4.1 ('TCCM is an inductive method ... unseen test data')
